clue.text: Depressed when involved in scrap? I can't be bothered!

indicators.note: being involved in something here means sitting inside the word for scrap

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit
depressed means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down after a fight shrugs off any further effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiomatic way of dismissing something as not worth the effort or trouble.

clue.text: Impressive person, endlessly calm and nobby

indicators.note: the word for calm is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lull is a calm period
U is the label for upper-class, posh or nobby usage

explanation.surface: A remarkable figure, unflappable and very posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes the last L off LULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is informal for an outstanding or remarkable person or thing.

clue.text: Comedian, fruity type, out of sorts and showing determination

parts.note: a wit is a humorous person, a joker
a haw is a type of fruit, the berry of the hawthorn
out of sorts means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A comic with a fondness for fruit feels unwell but presses on.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something energetically and resolutely is an idiom for showing determination.

clue.text: Capital investment, ultimately what must get managed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end of the word investment

parts.note: eh is said to mean what? when you mishear
to have run something is to have managed it

explanation.surface: Investment in the capital city needs careful management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts as money alongside 'investment', but it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: What sweat will do via pores in transformation

indicators.note: the letters of the two clue words undergo a transformation, being rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Perspiration escapes through the skin's pores and turns into vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat evaporates from the skin, turning into vapour, which is how it cools the body.

clue.text: One that's careering madly around is bitten by snake coming from plant

indicators.note: being bitten by the snake means sitting within its jaws, inside the snake's name

parts.note: the viper is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the letter for one, enclosing it
careering madly means the letters of careering are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something careering wildly about is bitten by a snake emerging from undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges CAREERING into RGINACREE, which 'around' wraps about I; 'is bitten by' then sets all of that between VI and PER. 'Plant' at the end is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a climbing vine noted for its red autumn foliage, a common garden plant.

clue.text: Quiet region of Spain's suitable for models

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
Aragon is a region in northeast Spain; the 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: The tranquil parts of Spain are ideal for fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Paragons are perfect examples, people held up as models to imitate.

clue.text: Reversible mechanical component

indicators.note: reversible here means the word reads the same when turned backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A machine part that can run either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine such as a helicopter or engine is a mechanical component.

clue.text: Feature of sweet thing that gypsy has inside

explanation.surface: A chocolate has a filling that a traveller hides.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: the middle letter of 'gypsy' is P, the musical sign for quiet, so gypsy has a soft centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate with a creamy filling has a soft middle; the word gypsy has P, meaning quiet, in the middle.

clue.text: Loud luster after women given time inside — ie one doing porridge

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: given inside means the letter for time is placed within the word for the womaniser

parts.note: a lecher is a man who lusts after women

explanation.surface: A noisy womaniser is jailed for a spell, a man doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is British slang for a prison sentence, and also the title of a classic BBC sitcom whose main character, the old lag, bears this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The convict Norman Stanley Fletcher is the jailbird hero of the prison sitcom Porridge.

clue.text: Approve, please, in the absence of leader

indicators.note: the synonym for please appears without its leading letter

parts.note: to please someone is to gratify them

explanation.surface: A polite request for approval, asked without a boss present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the absence of leader' removes G from GRATIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty or decision is to formally approve or sanction it.

clue.text: Enthusiasm in a periodical contest evokes song of praise

indicators.note: the word for enthusiasm goes inside the short word for a periodical

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical publication
zing is energy or enthusiasm
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A magazine competition run with gusto inspires a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known Christian hymn by John Newton is a song praising God's mercy.

clue.text: United v City? Not energy-packed, City!

parts.note: lo-cal, low in calories, means not packed with food energy
Derby is a city in the English East Midlands

explanation.surface: A football fan complains City are playing without any energy against United.
explanation.walkthrough: A local derby is a match between two teams from the same area, like Manchester United v Manchester City.
explanation.definitionFit: A match between two rival clubs from the same town is the classic local derby, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Native American greeting outside work

indicators.note: the greeting is placed outside, wrapping the short word for work

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A Native American says hello to someone outside a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are an indigenous people of northeastern Arizona.

clue.text: Unsuspecting pub taking old money

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A naive pub accepts payment in outdated currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Being guileless or naive, without suspicion of wrongdoing, is to be innocent.

clue.text: Be wound up in Home Counties party when entertained by comedian

indicators.note: being entertained by the comedian means sitting inside his name

parts.note: a clown is a comedian
SE, south-east, is where England's Home Counties around London lie
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party in the commuter belt turns tense when a comic performs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wound up in the sense of brought to an end is to close down, as a business does.

clue.text: Badly affected on account of strain in upsetting cricket practice

indicators.note: the word for strain goes inside the reversed practice word
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: nets are the netted practice areas used in cricket
to rick a joint is to strain or sprain it

explanation.surface: A player hurt himself pulling a muscle during a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' gives STEN, the reversal the parse turns; 'in' places the strain word within. Cricket nets are practice pitches enclosed by netting, a British sporting term.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stricken is severely afflicted or hit by illness or misfortune.

clue.text: Like some entertainment in the Globe? Then call back

parts.note: a ball is a globe, a sphere

indicators.note: back means the word for call is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite someone is to call or summon them, as to court

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer at Shakespeare's Globe is told to phone back later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CITE into ETIC. The Globe is the London theatre of Shakespeare's plays, which tempts towards drama rather than a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a form of stage entertainment, and balletic describes anything in that style.

clue.text: Jock's worthless bits kept in sporran

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the word sporran

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stores junk in the pouch worn with his kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A sporran is the pouch worn in front of a Scottish kilt; 'Jock' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means odd, spare or worthless, used of leftover scraps.

clue.text: Perfume always available in our second city

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the city's nickname

parts.note: Brum is the nickname for Birmingham, often called Britain's second city
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Fragrance is always on sale in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is widely called the UK's second city; Brum is its local nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fragrant lotion or cologne distilled from bay leaves with rum.

clue.text: Maybe you'll stick with this paper

definitions.text: Maybe you'll stick with this paper

parts.words: Maybe you'll stick with this paper
parts.note: read as loyalty to a newspaper, but it describes a sticky strip used to fasten paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper hopes its readers will remain loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky strip is what you use to fasten paper together or to a surface.

clue.text: One of our modern messages, half of them leading to trouble

indicators.note: half of means only the latter pair of letters of the word them is used

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Modern messaging causes problems half the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a characteristic message of our digital age.

clue.text: Leader of pilgrimage out of line, destroyed ultimately

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for out of line is destroyed

parts.note: askew means crooked, out of line

explanation.surface: The head of a religious procession strays and is finally ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Aske led the Pilgrimage of Grace, a Tudor rising against Henry VIII, and was executed in 1537.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Aske was the lawyer who led the 1536 northern rebellion known as the Pilgrimage of Grace.

clue.text: Strong drink makes one jeer, losing head

indicators.note: the word for jeer loses its first letter

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer or heckle

explanation.surface: A stiff drink makes someone heckle and lose their composure.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a strong spirit distilled in Asia from rice, palm sap or sugar cane.

clue.text: Creature sorry to be half-hearted, needing self-confidence

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its doubled middle vowel, is halved by losing one

parts.note: sorry in the sense of pitiful means poor
poise is composure and self-assurance

explanation.surface: Someone feeling sorry for themselves needs to regain their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be half-hearted' cuts the middle OO of POOR to a single O.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a small toothed whale, a marine mammal, so a creature.

clue.text: Maybe look at aeroplane's cosmetic product

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a liner, as in airliner, is a passenger aeroplane; the possessive gives no letter

explanation.surface: Glance at the aircraft's cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up drawn along the lashes is a cosmetic product for outlining the eyes.

clue.text: Hilary needs to get bloke on phone

parts.note: a bloke is a man
tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Hilary must get her man to call.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel was the novelist who wrote Wolf Hall, so the surname completes her name.
